lean.key_theorem: DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a_all (l in {2,3,4,5}, no hypothesis); also DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a_two / _three / _four / _five, DCTheoremA.frob_ev / step1 (Frobenius step, all l), DCTheoremA.content_coeff (integral multiples in Z[zeta]). DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a keeps Step2 l as an explicit hypothesis and is superseded by dc_theorem_a_all.
lean.faithfulness_note: Proved for l in {2,3,4,5}: dc_theorem_a_all has no hypothesis, no sorry, no new axiom. Statement: for l in {2,3,4,5}, p prime, a >= 1 (a >= 1 is not used, a = 0 is trivial), Phi_{p^a l} | S implies Phi_l | S in Z[q,q^-1], for every integer word w of any length; S is the recurrence S_{i+1}=[c_{i+1}]S_i-q^(c_i-1)S_{i-1} with (S_0,S_1)=(0,1) (previous quotient in the exponent). Structure: Step 1 (S(w^(p^a)) = S(w)^(p^a) + p*y with y an algebraic integer, any root of unity; frob_ev, step1). Step 2 (Step2 l: S_w(zeta) = p*y with y an algebraic integer implies S_w(zeta) = 0, zeta a primitive l-th root) is proved for each l by a finite closed set of coordinate states (S_{i-1}, S_i, c_i mod l) with S in integer power-basis coordinates of Z[zeta_l] (72, 96, 600 states for l = 3, 4, 5; 12 for l = 2), an evaluation-to-coordinates bridge (step_rel), and the content lemma content_coeff (uses that Z[zeta] is the integral closure of Z in Q(zeta), a point the write-up glosses: Step 1 yields an algebraic integer y, not an element of Z[zeta_l]). For l = 5 the candidate set is a literal produced outside Lean; soundness rests on the kernel-checked closure (Pk5_closed, Pk5_zero, Pk5_vals), not on the literal. Reviewer note: Step2 is a Lean-side formulation of the write-up's 'not in p Z[zeta_l]' claim.
lean.axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (for every theorem in the file, including dc_theorem_a_all)
lean.build_command: lake build Algebra.DCTheoremA (sandbox project requiring Mathlib v4.29.1)
lean.build_notes: Full-file check on macOS with /usr/bin/time -l lake env lean: 69 s wall, maximum resident set size 7,998,570,496 bytes; a file containing only 'import Mathlib' measures 5,271,044,096 bytes on the same machine (mostly memory-mapped Mathlib files), so the file adds roughly 2.7 GB. Single measurement each, LEAN_NUM_THREADS=2; not a precise peak. An earlier variant of the l = 5 check (membership by linear search in a 600-element list) was stopped by a resource guard above 9 GB, and the variant that ran the search inside the kernel was stopped above 13 GB; the search-tree lookup (KTree) is what made it fit.
